posts.title: Why Does Your Finger JUMP When You Close One Eye? 👁️
posts.caption:
Point at something... shut one eye... now the other. 👁️ Did your finger JUMP?
One eye is the boss: your brain aims with its picture. Shut the boss and you get the other eye's view, so the finger jumps.
Left or right?

posts.title: Why Does This Dot VANISH? (Find Your Blind Spot) 👁️
posts.caption:
Close your left eye, stare at the X... and bring your phone closer. 👁️ The red dot VANISHES.
Your eye has a hole: where the cable to your brain plugs in, there are no light sensors. Your brain just paints over the gap.
Did it vanish?

posts.title: Why Do You Feel TWO Noses? (Cross Your Fingers) 🤞
posts.caption:
Cross your fingers and rub your nose in the gap... two noses? 🤞👃
Your fingers swapped places and your brain never got the memo: a touch on both outside edges at once has always meant two things.
One nose or two?

posts.title: Can You ROLL Your Tongue? (It's Not Just Genes) 👅
posts.caption:
Can you roll your tongue? Try it right now... 👅
Can't? Don't blame your parents: identical twins have the same genes, and one can while the other can't. It was never one gene.
Yes or no?

posts.title: Why Does Your Foot FLIP When You Draw a 6? 🦶
posts.caption:
Circle your right foot clockwise and draw a 6 with your right hand... 🦶
Your foot flips, right? Your right hand and foot share a boss (the left side of your brain), and it wants them going the same way. Try the 6 with your LEFT hand: easier.
Did it flip? Yes or no?

posts.title: Why Can't You HUM With Your Nose Pinched? 🤐
posts.caption:
Hum along... then pinch your nose shut. 🤐
Your hum dies, right? A hum is air leaving through your nose with your lips shut. Pinch it and the air piles up until it pushes back as hard as your lungs: no flow, no buzz.
Did your hum stop? Yes or no?

posts.title: Why Can't You Breathe and SWALLOW at the Same Time? 🫁
posts.caption:
Swallow... and breathe in at the SAME time. 🫁
Air and spit share ONE tunnel: on every swallow your brain pauses your breathing and a little lid slams over your windpipe.
Could you?

posts.title: Why Is the Vulcan Salute So HARD? 🖖
posts.caption:
Try the Vulcan salute: split your fingers, two and two. 🖖
Your middle and ring fingers are holding hands under your skin: their cords are strapped together, and your brain moves them as a team.
Can you split your fingers?

posts.title: Why Is There a SAUSAGE Between Your Fingers? 🌭
posts.caption:
Touch your fingertips together near your eyes... now look PAST them. 🌭
That floating sausage? You're seeing double: each eye sees your fingers from its own side, and your brain stacks the two pictures anyway.
Did you see it?

posts.title: Why Can't You TICKLE Yourself? (Try It Now) 🤭
posts.caption:
Try to tickle your own palm. Right now. 🤭
Nothing? Your brain read the spoiler: it keeps a copy of every move you make, so it knows exactly where your finger lands and turns the feeling down. Someone else's finger comes with no warning.
Did it tickle?

posts.title: Why Do Some People Have NO Wrist Tendon? 🖐️
posts.caption:
Touch your thumb to your pinky... and bend your wrist. 🖐️
See a cord pop up? That's a muscle your body forgot to delete. About 1 in 7 people don't have it, sometimes in just one arm, and they grip just as hard. Surgeons even use it to rebuild baseball pitchers' elbows.
Did a cord pop up? Yes or no?

posts.title: Why Can't You Raise Just ONE Eyebrow? 🤨
posts.caption:
Raise just ONE of your eyebrows. 🤨
Both went up, right? Each half of your brain pulls a string tied to BOTH brows, but your mouth gets one string per side: that's why half a smile is easy.
Could you raise just one? Yes or no?

posts.title: Why Can't Most People WIGGLE Their Ears? 👂
posts.caption:
Wiggle your ears. No eyebrows! 👂
Nope? Your brain lost the remote for them about 25 million years ago, so it mashes your eyebrows instead. But the 3 tiny muscles on each ear still twitch when a sound comes from one side.
Could you wiggle them? Yes or no?
